 Dated this the 12th day of November, 2024  ORDER
This is an application for regular bail moved by the first accused in crime No.260/2024 of Kadakkal Police Station, Kollam.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the relevant documents form part of the case diary.

3. The prosecution case is that on 27.01.2024, the petitioner herein persuaded the defacto complainant to reach the house of the petitioner and when the defacto complainant reached therein,
the petitioner along with the 1st accused, out of their common intention, attacked the defacto complainant with intention to commit her murder.

The specific allegation is that the petitioner and the 1 st accused wrongfully restrained her and voluntarily caused hurt to her by stabbing her with a knife and 2024:KER:85354 thereby attempted to commit murder.
On the above premise, crime was registered alleging commission of offences punishable under Sections 323, 324, 341, 307 and 506(ii), 307 r/w Section 34 of Indian Penal Code.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner, who is the 1 st accused in this crime, would submit that as per Annexure-6 order in B.ANo.3909 dated 27.05.2024 this Court granted regular bail to the 2nd accused.
It is submitted that the anticipatory bail application filed by the petitioner was dismissed by this Court on 30.08.2024 as per Annexure 4 order.
The petitioner has been in custody from 10.09.2024 onwards and therefore the petitioner may be released on bail.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the petitioner surrendered before the police on 10.09.2024 after dismissal of his anticipatory bail application and has been in custody thereafter for about two months and therefore he deserves bail.
5. Whereas it is submitted by the learned Public Prosecutor that the 2nd accused was granted bail by this Court taking note of the fact that he is a first time offender.

According to the learned Public Prosecutor, the petitioner is a person, aged 37 years, who has involvement in 8 crimes apart from the present crime of very serious nature, and, therefore, his 2024:KER:85354 release on bail may result in involvement of the petitioner in further crimes.
Therefore, this matter would require trial keeping him in custody.

6. In Annexure A4 anticipatory bail order, whereby the petitioner's anticipatory bail was denied by this Court his involvement in 8 crimes are extracted as under:
"1. Pangode P.S., crime No.31/2018, u/s 450, 376 IPC, 4 r/w 3 of POCSO Act.
2. Chithara P.S., crime No.95/2024, u/s 498(A), 323, 324, 294(b) and 34 IPC.

2
3. Kadakkal P.S., crime No.599/2009, u/s 323, 294(b), 308 and 34 IPC.
4. Kadakkal P.S., crime No.133/2015, u/s 380 IPC.
5. Kadakkal P.S., crime No.7/2008, u/s 342, 324, 506(ii), 294(b) IPC.
6. Chithara P.S., crime No.870/2021, u/s 498(A), 342, 34 IPC.
8. Valiyamala P.S., crime No.77/2018, u/s 376 IPC."

7. Going by the prosecution allegations, the prosecution case is that the petitioner/1st accused wrongfully restrained the defacto complainant, voluntarily caused hurt to her by stabbing her with a knife and thereby attempted to commit murder.

The prosecution case is made 2024:KER:85354 out,
prima facie.

Addressing the involvement of the petitioner in 8 crimes, those are crimes of serious nature, including offences under Sections 376, 380, 498A, 307, 308 and 326 of IPC as well as under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (`POCSO Act').

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is relevant to note that he has involvement in one crime where aggravated penetrative sexual assault was alleged and thereby he alleged to have committed offence punishable under Section 4 read with 3 of the POCSO Act.
The offence involved in the 8th crime committed by him is also punishable under Section 376 of IPC.

Thus it appears that the petitioner is a habitual offender having involvement in 9 crimes altogether,
where he alleged to have committed very serious offences.
He would repeat similar crimes and stall the trial, if he would be released on bail.
Though the 2 nd accused was granted regular bail by this Court, the same was on the finding that the 2nd accused was a first time offender.
Therefore, this bail application is liable to fail and is accordingly dismissed.
